mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix definition allows the model to invent arbitrary permissions, which violates the least-privilege and permission-grounding assertions that depend on the matrix being correctly specified.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidPermission { Officer -> PostApplications in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the non-empty-universe constraint allows the model to satisfy audit-related predicates vacuously (since they quantify over empty sets). The injection forces at least one audit entry to exist so the assertions must actually constrain structure.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_EmptyUniverse { some u: User, app: LoanApplication, entry: AuditEntry | entry.application = app }

mutation_targets.rationale: The NoSelfMutation assertion requires audit entries where the actor_role is Officer to have actor != app.applicant. If we allow an officer to submit their own application (by removing the permission matrix constraint), we can construct a violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfMutation { some app: LoanApplication, entry: AuditEntry | entry.application = app and entry.actor_role = Officer and entry.actor = app.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: These assertions require at least one application to exist. Removing the non-empty constraint lets them pass vacuously. The injection forces a violation of the one-in-flight rule.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleInFlight { some u: User, disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.applicant = u and a2.applicant = u and a1.status = Pending and a2.status = Pending }

mutation_targets.rationale: The AppendOnly assertion requires at least one audit entry to validate that all entries are distinct. Removing non-empty allows it to pass vacuously. The injection creates a duplicate entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateAudit { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.actor_role = e2.actor_role and e1.new_status = e2.new_status }
